title: the WSG rope - crossing a chasm
audit_label: R445 WSG chasm crossing pin audit
audit_comment: The chasm-crossing slice pins the two anchor factors (a protrusion to anchor on, an anchor that holds - the grappling hook answers both via Table 20), the thrown-loop tactic (thief or rope-use proficient only, target directly across or slightly above/below, never on a vertical climb), Table 21 THROWN LOOP RANGES (40/50/60/75/90 feet by level band), the 10-foot whirl-radius assumption with the halved range otherwise, the 20% base hit chance with the +1% closeness bonus per foot below maximum range, the halving conditions (moderate to heavy precipitation, wind over 20 mph, hampered visibility), the both-ends-anchored rule with the near-side protrusion requirement, and the 30-feet-per-round hand-over-hand crossing rate with the +2 Dexterity check for multiple simultaneous hangers (rules/wsgchasm.h, prefix wcx); census 369 -> 370.

banner.title: The WSG CROSSING A CHASM ON A ROPE, R445: the chasm prose and Table 21 - characters can negotiate a chasm or deep canyon by anchoring a rope on the far side and moving hand-over-hand across it. Success depends on two factors: whether the terrain offers a protrusion to anchor a line, and whether the rope can be anchored to hold their weight; a grappling hook answers both questions through Table 20. A thrown loop of rope can also catch a protrusion if the target is directly across or only slightly above or below the thrower (never on a vertical climb), but only a thief or a rope-use proficient character can succeed. Table 21 gives the maximum ranges by level band: 40 feet at 1-4, 50 at 5-8, 60 at 9-12, 75 at 13-16 and 90 at 17+. The ranges assume a clear 10-foot radius to whirl the loop; without it, half the given figure. The base chance of hitting the target is 20%, plus 1% for every foot of distance below the maximum range; moderate to heavy precipitation, wind over 20 miles per hour or hampered visibility (fog, night) halve the chance - the fog example: a 17th-level character at 50 feet has (20 + 40) / 2 = 30%. Before crossing, BOTH ends must be anchored, and a suitable protrusion must exist on the near side too (wise to check before anchoring the far side). Once anchored, characters move hand-over-hand at a maximum 30 feet per round; it is prudent for only one to use the rope at a time - if more than one hangs from it, each makes a Dexterity Check at +2 on the die, failure meaning a lost grip and a fall. Census 369 -> 370.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed pp. 38-39; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0038.djvu for the chasm prose and Table 21, the Guide_0039.djvu head for the crossing rate) - the section reads CLEAN, every number (the 40/50/60/75/90 ranges, the 10-foot radius, the 20% base with the +1% per foot, the 20 mph wind, the 17th-level 30% fog example, the 30-feet-per-round rate and the +2 Dexterity modifier) matched exactly; no eye-reads were needed.
banner.sentinel: The thrown loop: 40 to 90 feet by level band, base hit chance 20% plus 1% per foot below maximum range, halved in bad conditions - and the crossing itself runs hand-over-hand at 30 feet per round, one character at a time, with a +2 Dexterity Check for each extra hanger on the rope.

consts.name: wcxBaseHitPct
consts.comment: The base chance of hitting the target with a thrown loop is 20%.

consts.name: wcxClosenessBonusPerFt
consts.comment: The hit chance gains a +1% bonus for every foot of distance between thrower and target that is LESS than the maximum range - the closer the target, the better the chance.

consts.name: wcxWhirlRadiusFt
consts.comment: The Table 21 ranges assume a clear 10-foot radius of space around the character so the loop can be whirled around before it is released.

consts.name: wcxWindMphLimit
consts.comment: Wind blowing more than 20 miles per hour halves the chance of hitting the target; moderate to heavy precipitation or hampered visibility (fog, night) do the same.

consts.name: wcxCrossRateFtPerRound
consts.comment: Once a rope is securely anchored at both ends, characters move along it hand-over-hand at a maximum rate of 30 feet per round.

consts.name: wcxMultipleHangerDexMod
consts.comment: If more than one character hangs from the rope at the same time, each of them must make a Dexterity Check with a +2 modifier to the die roll; failure means a lost grip and a fall.

consts.name: wcxLoopBandCount
consts.comment: Table 21 has five level bands: 1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16 and 17+.

bools.name: wcxTwoFactorsProtrusionAndHold
bools.comment: The chasm tactic depends on two factors: whether the terrain offers a protrusion to anchor a line, and whether the rope can be anchored so it will hold the characters weight.

bools.name: wcxGrapplingHookViaTable20
bools.comment: A rope attached to a grappling hook answers both factors by using Table 20, choosing the terrain line that most closely corresponds to the target area.

bools.name: wcxLoopTargetAcrossOrSlightly
bools.comment: A thrown loop can catch a protrusion only if the target is located directly across from or only slightly above or below the thrower.

bools.name: wcxLoopNeverOnVerticalClimb
bools.comment: The thrown-loop tactic does not work on a vertical climb, which is why it was not discussed with the grappling hooks.

bools.name: wcxThiefOrRopeUseOnly
bools.comment: Only a thief or a character with proficiency in rope use can succeed with a thrown loop; no one else can.

bools.name: wcxNoWhirlRadiusHalvesRange
bools.comment: Without the clear 10-foot whirling radius, the maximum range is half of the given Table 21 figure.

bools.name: wcxBadConditionsHalveHit
bools.comment: Moderate to heavy precipitation, wind over 20 miles per hour, or any condition hampering visibility (fog, night) modifies the hit chance downward by half.

bools.name: wcxBothEndsMustBeAnchored
bools.comment: Before characters can move across a horizontally anchored rope, both ends must be anchored - which means a suitable protrusion must also exist at the location the characters are moving FROM (wise to check before anchoring the far side).

bools.name: wcxOneAtATimePrudent
bools.comment: It is prudent for only one character to use the rope at a time.

bools.name: wcxMultiHangerDexCheck
bools.comment: If more than one character hangs from the rope at the same time, each must make the +2 Dexterity Check; failure means the character loses his grip on the rope and falls.

tables.name: Table 21: THROWN LOOP RANGES
tables.audit_comment: the Table 21 grid: the five level bands (1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16, 17+) x the maximum thrown-loop range in feet - 40/50/60/75/90, with the 17+ band continuing beyond the table
col_comments: The maximum distance in feet at which the character can hit a target with a thrown loop, by level band: 40 feet at levels 1-4, 50 at 5-8, 60 at 9-12, 75 at 13-16 and 90 at 17 and above.

the whirl-radius halving: without the 10-foot radius the range is half the given figure - the 1-4 band drops from 40 to 20 feet

table_checks.expr: m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](0) >= m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](1) or m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](1) >= m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](2) or m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](2) >= m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](3) or m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](3) >= m['wcxMaxRangeFt'](4)
table_checks.note: the thrown-loop range is strictly increasing by level band - experience extends the reach
the top-band step: the range gains exactly 15 feet at each of the top two bands (60 -> 75 -> 90)
the 17+ band bound: 90 feet of thrown range - exactly three rounds of the 30-feet-per-round hand-over-hand crossing
